title: What Makes a Good Life? Lessons from the Longest Study on Happiness | Robert Waldinger | TED

blocks.en_text: What keeps us healthy and happy
blocks.zh_text: 是什么让我们在人生中保持健康和快乐

blocks.en_text: as we go through life?
blocks.zh_text: 在我们走过一生的时候？

blocks.en_text: If you were going to invest now
blocks.zh_text: 如果你现在要投资

blocks.en_text: in your future best self,
blocks.zh_text: 在未来最好的自己身上，

blocks.en_text: where would you put your time and your energy?
blocks.zh_text: 你会把时间和精力花在哪里？

blocks.en_text: There was a recent survey of millennials
blocks.zh_text: 最近有一项针对千禧一代的调查

blocks.en_text: asking them what their most important life goals were,
blocks.zh_text: 问他们最重要的人生目标是什么，

blocks.en_text: and over 80 percent said
blocks.zh_text: 超过80%的人说

blocks.en_text: that a major life goal for them was to get rich.
blocks.zh_text: 他们的一个重要人生目标就是变得富有。

blocks.en_text: And another 50 percent of those same young adults
blocks.zh_text: 而这些同样的年轻人中还有50%

blocks.en_text: said that another major life goal
blocks.zh_text: 说另一个重要的人生目标

blocks.en_text: was to become famous.
blocks.zh_text: 是出名。

blocks.en_text: And we're constantly told to lean in to work, to push harder
blocks.zh_text: 我们不断被告知要投入工作，要更加努力

blocks.en_text: and achieve more.
blocks.zh_text: 取得更多成就。

blocks.en_text: We're given the impression that these are the things that we need to go after
blocks.zh_text: 我们得到的印象是，这些就是我们必须要追求的东西

blocks.en_text: in order to have a good life.
blocks.zh_text: 为了拥有美好的生活。

blocks.en_text: Pictures of entire lives,
blocks.zh_text: 完整人生的画面，

blocks.en_text: of the choices that people make and how those choices work out for them,
blocks.zh_text: 人们所做的选择以及这些选择给他们带来的结果，

blocks.en_text: those pictures are almost impossible to get.
blocks.zh_text: 这些画面几乎是不可能得到的。

blocks.en_text: Most of what we know about human life
blocks.zh_text: 我们对人类生活的大部分了解

blocks.en_text: we know from asking people to remember the past,
blocks.zh_text: 都来自让人们回忆过去，

blocks.en_text: and as we know, hindsight is anything but 20/20.
blocks.zh_text: 而众所周知，事后诸葛亮可一点都不靠谱。

blocks.en_text: We forget vast amounts of what happens to us in life,
blocks.zh_text: 我们会忘记生活中发生的大量事情，

blocks.en_text: and sometimes memory is downright creative.
blocks.zh_text: 有时候记忆还相当有创造性。

blocks.en_text: But what if we could watch entire lives
blocks.zh_text: 但如果我们能观察完整的人生

blocks.en_text: as they unfold through time?
blocks.zh_text: 随着时间展开呢？

blocks.en_text: What if we could study people from the time that they were teenagers
blocks.zh_text: 如果我们能从人们还是青少年的时候就开始研究他们

blocks.en_text: all the way into old age
blocks.zh_text: 一直追踪到老年

blocks.en_text: to see what really keeps people happy and healthy?
blocks.zh_text: 看看究竟是什么让人们真正保持快乐和健康呢？

blocks.en_text: We did that.
blocks.zh_text: 我们做到了。

blocks.en_text: The Harvard Study of Adult Development
blocks.zh_text: 哈佛成人发展研究

blocks.en_text: may be the longest study of adult life that's ever been done.
blocks.zh_text: 可能是有史以来进行过的最长的成人生活研究。

blocks.en_text: For 75 years, we've tracked the lives of 724 men,
blocks.zh_text: 75年来，我们追踪了724名男性的生活，

blocks.en_text: year after year, asking about their work, their home lives, their health,
blocks.zh_text: 年复一年，询问他们的工作、家庭生活、健康状况，

blocks.en_text: and of course asking all along the way without knowing how their life stories
blocks.zh_text: 当然一路上都在问，却不知道他们的人生故事

blocks.en_text: were going to turn out.
blocks.zh_text: 最终会怎样发展。

blocks.en_text: Studies like this are exceedingly rare.
blocks.zh_text: 像这样的研究极其罕见。

blocks.en_text: Almost all projects of this kind fall apart within a decade
blocks.zh_text: 几乎所有这类项目都在十年内瓦解

blocks.en_text: because too many people drop out of the study,
blocks.zh_text: 因为太多人退出研究，

blocks.en_text: or funding for the research dries up,
blocks.zh_text: 或者研究经费枯竭，

blocks.en_text: or the researchers get distracted,
blocks.zh_text: 或者研究人员分心了，

blocks.en_text: or they die, and nobody moves the ball further down the field.
blocks.zh_text: 或者他们去世了，没有人再把这件事往前推进。

blocks.en_text: But through a combination of luck
blocks.zh_text: 但靠着运气的结合

blocks.en_text: and the persistence of several generations of researchers,
blocks.zh_text: 以及几代研究人员的坚持，

blocks.en_text: this study has survived.
blocks.zh_text: 这项研究存活了下来。

blocks.en_text: About 60 of our original 724 men
blocks.zh_text: 我们最初724名男性中大约有60人

blocks.en_text: are still alive,
blocks.zh_text: 仍然在世，

blocks.en_text: still participating in the study,
blocks.zh_text: 仍在参与这项研究，

blocks.en_text: most of them in their 90s.
blocks.zh_text: 他们大多已经九十多岁了。

blocks.en_text: And we are now beginning to study
blocks.zh_text: 而我们现在开始研究

blocks.en_text: the more than 2,000 children of these men.
blocks.zh_text: 这些人的两千多名子女。

blocks.en_text: And I'm the fourth director of the study.
blocks.zh_text: 我是这项研究的第四任负责人。

blocks.en_text: Since 1938, we've tracked the lives of two groups of men.
blocks.zh_text: 从1938年起，我们追踪了两组男性的生活。

blocks.en_text: The first group started in the study
blocks.zh_text: 第一组人在研究开始时

blocks.en_text: when they were sophomores at Harvard College.
blocks.zh_text: 还是哈佛学院的大二学生。

blocks.en_text: They all finished college during World War II,
blocks.zh_text: 他们都在二战期间读完了大学，

blocks.en_text: and then most went off to serve in the war.
blocks.zh_text: 之后大多数人去参了战。

blocks.en_text: And the second group that we've followed
blocks.zh_text: 我们追踪的第二组人

blocks.en_text: was a group of boys from Boston's poorest neighborhoods,
blocks.zh_text: 是一群来自波士顿最贫困街区的男孩，

blocks.en_text: boys who were chosen for the study
blocks.zh_text: 这些男孩之所以被选入研究，

blocks.en_text: specifically because they were from some of the most troubled
blocks.zh_text: 正是因为他们来自一些最麻烦

blocks.en_text: and disadvantaged families
blocks.zh_text: 、最弱势的家庭，

blocks.en_text: in the Boston of the 1930s.
blocks.zh_text: 那是20世纪30年代的波士顿。

blocks.en_text: Most lived in tenements, many without hot and cold running water.
blocks.zh_text: 他们大多住在廉租房里，很多人家里连冷热水都没有。

blocks.en_text: When they entered the study,
blocks.zh_text: 他们刚加入研究时，

blocks.en_text: all of these teenagers were interviewed.
blocks.zh_text: 所有这些青少年都接受了访谈。

blocks.en_text: They were given medical exams.
blocks.zh_text: 他们做了体检。

blocks.en_text: We went to their homes and we interviewed their parents.
blocks.zh_text: 我们去他们家，采访了他们的父母。

blocks.en_text: And then these teenagers grew up into adults
blocks.zh_text: 后来这些青少年长大成人，

blocks.en_text: who entered all walks of life.
blocks.zh_text: 进入了各行各业。

blocks.en_text: They became factory workers and lawyers and bricklayers and doctors,
blocks.zh_text: 他们成了工厂工人、律师、砖瓦匠和医生，

blocks.en_text: one President of the United States.
blocks.zh_text: 其中一位还当上了美国总统。

blocks.en_text: Some developed alcoholism. A few developed schizophrenia.
blocks.zh_text: 有些人患上了酗酒。有几个人得了精神分裂症。

blocks.en_text: Some climbed the social ladder
blocks.zh_text: 有些人沿着社会阶梯往上爬，

blocks.en_text: from the bottom all the way to the very top,
blocks.zh_text: 从最底层一路爬到最顶层，

blocks.en_text: and some made that journey in the opposite direction.
blocks.zh_text: 也有些人走的是相反的方向。

blocks.en_text: The founders of this study
blocks.zh_text: 这项研究的创始人

blocks.en_text: would never in their wildest dreams
blocks.zh_text: 做梦也想不到

blocks.en_text: have imagined that I would be standing here today, 75 years later,
blocks.zh_text: 75年后的今天，我会站在这里，

blocks.en_text: telling you that the study still continues.
blocks.zh_text: 告诉你们这项研究仍在继续。

blocks.en_text: Every two years, our patient and dedicated research staff
blocks.zh_text: 每两年，我们耐心而敬业的研究人员

blocks.en_text: calls up our men and asks them if we can send them
blocks.zh_text: 就会给我们的研究对象打电话，问能不能再给他们寄

blocks.en_text: yet one more set of questions about their lives.
blocks.zh_text: 一套关于他们生活的问题。

blocks.en_text: Many of the inner city Boston men ask us,
blocks.zh_text: 波士顿市中心的很多男性会问我们：

blocks.en_text: "Why do you keep wanting to study me? My life just isn't that interesting."
blocks.zh_text: “你们为什么老想研究我？我的生活真没那么有意思。”

blocks.en_text: The Harvard men never ask that question.
blocks.zh_text: 哈佛那组人从来不问这个问题。

blocks.en_text: To get the clearest picture of these lives,
blocks.zh_text: 为了最清楚地了解这些人的生活，

blocks.en_text: we don't just send them questionnaires.
blocks.zh_text: 我们不只是给他们寄问卷。

blocks.en_text: We interview them in their living rooms.
blocks.zh_text: 我们在他们的客厅里采访他们。

blocks.en_text: We get their medical records from their doctors.
blocks.zh_text: 我们从他们的医生那里获取病历。

blocks.en_text: We draw their blood, we scan their brains,
blocks.zh_text: 我们给他们抽血，扫描他们的大脑，

blocks.en_text: we talk to their children.
blocks.zh_text: 我们和他们的孩子交谈。

blocks.en_text: We videotape them talking with their wives about their deepest concerns.
blocks.zh_text: 我们录下他们和妻子谈论内心最深处的担忧。

blocks.en_text: And when, about a decade ago, we finally asked the wives
blocks.zh_text: 大约十年前，我们终于问这些妻子

blocks.en_text: if they would join us as members of the study,
blocks.zh_text: 是否愿意作为研究成员加入我们。

blocks.en_text: many of the women said, "You know, it's about time."
blocks.zh_text: 很多女性都说：“你知道，早就该这样了。”

blocks.en_text: So what have we learned?
blocks.zh_text: 那么，我们学到了什么？

blocks.en_text: What are the lessons that come from the tens of thousands of pages
blocks.zh_text: 从成千上万页的资料中，我们能得到什么启示？

blocks.en_text: of information that we've generated
blocks.zh_text: 这些资料都是我们积累下来的，

blocks.en_text: on these lives?
blocks.zh_text: 关于这些人的一生。

blocks.en_text: Well, the lessons aren't about wealth or fame or working harder and harder.
blocks.zh_text: 这些启示与财富、名声，或者拼命工作无关。

blocks.en_text: The clearest message that we get from this 75-year study is this:
blocks.zh_text: 这项长达75年的研究给我们最明确的结论是：

blocks.en_text: Good relationships keep us happier and healthier. Period.
blocks.zh_text: 良好的人际关系让我们更快乐、更健康。就是这样。

blocks.en_text: We've learned three big lessons about relationships.
blocks.zh_text: 关于人际关系，我们学到了三大启示。

blocks.en_text: The first is that social connections are really good for us,
blocks.zh_text: 第一，社会联系对我们真的很有好处，

blocks.en_text: and that loneliness kills.
blocks.zh_text: 而孤独会致命。

blocks.en_text: It turns out that people who are more socially connected
blocks.zh_text: 事实证明，与家人、朋友、社区联系更紧密的人，

blocks.en_text: to family, to friends, to community,
blocks.zh_text: 与家人、朋友、社区联系更紧密的人，

blocks.en_text: are happier, they're physically healthier, and they live longer
blocks.zh_text: 更快乐，身体更健康，也活得更长，

blocks.en_text: than people who are less well connected.
blocks.zh_text: 比那些联系较少的人活得更长。

blocks.en_text: And the experience of loneliness turns out to be toxic.
blocks.zh_text: 而孤独的体验，事实证明是有害的。

blocks.en_text: People who are more isolated than they want to be from others
blocks.zh_text: 那些比自己所希望的更孤立于他人的人

blocks.en_text: find that they are less happy,
blocks.zh_text: 会发现自己没那么快乐，

blocks.en_text: their health declines earlier in midlife,
blocks.zh_text: 健康在中年时更早衰退，

blocks.en_text: their brain functioning declines sooner
blocks.zh_text: 大脑功能更早衰退，

blocks.en_text: and they live shorter lives than people who are not lonely.
blocks.zh_text: 而且比不孤独的人活得更短。

blocks.en_text: And the sad fact is that at any given time,
blocks.zh_text: 而令人难过的是，在任何时候，

blocks.en_text: more than one in five Americans will report that they're lonely.
blocks.zh_text: 超过五分之一的美国人会说自己感到孤独。

blocks.en_text: And we know that you can be lonely in a crowd
blocks.zh_text: 我们知道，你可以在人群中感到孤独，

blocks.en_text: and you can be lonely in a marriage,
blocks.zh_text: 也可以在婚姻中感到孤独，

blocks.en_text: so the second big lesson that we learned
blocks.zh_text: 所以我们学到的第二大启示

blocks.en_text: is that it's not just the number of friends you have,
blocks.zh_text: 是，重要的不只是你有多少朋友，

blocks.en_text: and it's not whether or not you're in a committed relationship,
blocks.zh_text: 也不在于你是否处于一段稳定的感情关系中，

blocks.en_text: but it's the quality of your close relationships that matters.
blocks.zh_text: 而是你亲密关系的质量才重要。

blocks.en_text: It turns out that living in the midst of conflict is really bad for our health.
blocks.zh_text: 事实证明，生活在冲突之中对我们的健康非常有害。

blocks.en_text: High-conflict marriages, for example, without much affection,
blocks.zh_text: 比如，缺乏温情的、冲突激烈的婚姻，

blocks.en_text: turn out to be very bad for our health, perhaps worse than getting divorced.
blocks.zh_text: 对我们的健康非常有害，也许比离婚还糟。

blocks.en_text: And living in the midst of good, warm relationships is protective.
blocks.zh_text: 而生活在良好、温暖的关系中则具有保护作用。

blocks.en_text: Once we had followed our men all the way into their 80s,
blocks.zh_text: 当我们一直追踪这些人到他们80多岁时，

blocks.en_text: we wanted to look back at them at midlife
blocks.zh_text: 我们想回头看看他们中年时的状况

blocks.en_text: and to see if we could predict
blocks.zh_text: 看看我们能否预测

blocks.en_text: who was going to grow into a happy, healthy octogenarian
blocks.zh_text: 谁会成长为快乐、健康的八旬老人

blocks.en_text: and who wasn't.
blocks.zh_text: 谁不会。

blocks.en_text: And when we gathered together everything we knew about them
blocks.zh_text: 当我们把他们50岁时

blocks.en_text: at age 50,
blocks.zh_text: 我们所知道的一切汇总起来时，

blocks.en_text: it wasn't their middle age cholesterol levels
blocks.zh_text: 并不是他们中年的胆固醇水平

blocks.en_text: that predicted how they were going to grow old.
blocks.zh_text: 预测了他们将如何变老。

blocks.en_text: It was how satisfied they were in their relationships.
blocks.zh_text: 而是他们对自己关系的满意程度。

blocks.en_text: The people who were the most satisfied in their relationships at age 50
blocks.zh_text: 那些在50岁时对人际关系最满意的人

blocks.en_text: were the healthiest at age 80.
blocks.zh_text: 在80岁时是最健康的。

blocks.en_text: And good, close relationships seem to buffer us
blocks.zh_text: 而良好、亲密的关系似乎能帮我们缓冲

blocks.en_text: from some of the slings and arrows of getting old.
blocks.zh_text: 衰老带来的种种打击和伤害。

blocks.en_text: Our most happily partnered men and women
blocks.zh_text: 我们那些伴侣关系最幸福的男男女女

blocks.en_text: reported, in their 80s,
blocks.zh_text: 在80多岁时表示，

blocks.en_text: that on the days when they had more physical pain,
blocks.zh_text: 在身体疼痛较多的那些日子里，

blocks.en_text: their mood stayed just as happy.
blocks.zh_text: 他们的心情依然一样快乐。

blocks.en_text: But the people who were in unhappy relationships,
blocks.zh_text: 但那些处在不幸福关系中的人，

blocks.en_text: on the days when they reported more physical pain,
blocks.zh_text: 在报告身体疼痛较多的那些日子里，

blocks.en_text: it was magnified by more emotional pain.
blocks.zh_text: 这种疼痛还会被更多的情绪痛苦放大。

blocks.en_text: And the third big lesson that we learned about relationships and our health
blocks.zh_text: 而我们关于人际关系与健康学到的第三个重要道理

blocks.en_text: is that good relationships don't just protect our bodies,
blocks.zh_text: 就是良好的人际关系不仅保护我们的身体，

blocks.en_text: they protect our brains.
blocks.zh_text: 也保护我们的大脑。

blocks.en_text: It turns out that being in a securely attached relationship
blocks.zh_text: 事实证明，在80多岁时拥有一段

blocks.en_text: to another person in your 80s is protective,
blocks.zh_text: 与他人安全依恋的关系是有保护作用的，

blocks.en_text: that the people who are in relationships
blocks.zh_text: 那些处在这样的关系中的人，

blocks.en_text: where they really feel they can count on the other person in times of need,
blocks.zh_text: 也就是真正觉得在需要时可以依靠对方的人，

blocks.en_text: those people's memories stay sharper longer.
blocks.zh_text: 这些人的记忆力保持得更敏锐、更长久。

blocks.en_text: And the people in relationships
blocks.zh_text: 而那些处在这样的关系中的人，

blocks.en_text: where they feel they really can't count on the other one,
blocks.zh_text: 也就是觉得自己真的无法依靠对方的人，

blocks.en_text: those are the people who experience earlier memory decline.
blocks.zh_text: 这些人会更早出现记忆力衰退。

blocks.en_text: And those good relationships, they don't have to be smooth all the time.
blocks.zh_text: 而那些良好的关系，也不必时时刻刻都一帆风顺。

blocks.en_text: Some of our octogenarian couples could bicker with each other
blocks.zh_text: 我们有些八十多岁的夫妻会互相拌嘴，

blocks.en_text: day in and day out,
blocks.zh_text: 天天如此，

blocks.en_text: but as long as they felt that they could really count on the other
blocks.zh_text: 但只要他们觉得在困难的时候

blocks.en_text: when the going got tough,
blocks.zh_text: 真的可以依靠对方，

blocks.en_text: those arguments didn't take a toll on their memories.
blocks.zh_text: 那些争吵就不会损害他们的记忆力。

blocks.en_text: So this message,
blocks.zh_text: 所以这个道理，

blocks.en_text: that good, close relationships are good for our health and well-being,
blocks.zh_text: 也就是良好、亲密的关系有益于我们的健康和幸福，

blocks.en_text: this is wisdom that's as old as the hills.
blocks.zh_text: 这是古老得不能再古老的智慧。

blocks.en_text: Why is this so hard to get and so easy to ignore?
blocks.zh_text: 为什么它这么难以领会，又这么容易被忽视呢？

blocks.en_text: Well, we're human.
blocks.zh_text: 嗯，因为我们是人。

blocks.en_text: What we'd really like is a quick fix,
blocks.zh_text: 我们真正想要的是一劳永逸的解决办法，

blocks.en_text: something we can get
blocks.zh_text: 是某种我们能得到的东西，

blocks.en_text: that'll make our lives good and keep them that way.
blocks.zh_text: 能让我们的生活变好，并一直保持下去。

blocks.en_text: Relationships are messy and they're complicated
blocks.zh_text: 人际关系是凌乱的，也是复杂的，

blocks.en_text: and the hard work of tending to family and friends,
blocks.zh_text: 而用心经营家人和朋友关系的辛苦付出，

blocks.en_text: it's not sexy or glamorous.
blocks.zh_text: 既不性感，也不光鲜。

blocks.en_text: It's also lifelong. It never ends.
blocks.zh_text: 它还是一辈子的事，永远没有尽头。

blocks.en_text: The people in our 75-year study who were the happiest in retirement
blocks.zh_text: 在我们这项长达75年的研究中，退休后最幸福的人

blocks.en_text: were the people who had actively worked to replace workmates with new playmates.
blocks.zh_text: 是那些主动努力用新玩伴取代工作伙伴的人。

blocks.en_text: Just like the millennials in that recent survey,
blocks.zh_text: 就像最近那项调查中的千禧一代一样，

blocks.en_text: many of our men when they were starting out as young adults
blocks.zh_text: 我们的许多男性在刚步入成年时

blocks.en_text: really believed that fame and wealth and high achievement
blocks.zh_text: 真的相信名望、财富和很高的成就

blocks.en_text: were what they needed to go after to have a good life.
blocks.zh_text: 才是他们为了过上好日子必须去追求的东西。

blocks.en_text: But over and over, over these 75 years, our study has shown
blocks.zh_text: 但在这75年里，我们的研究一次又一次地表明

blocks.en_text: that the people who fared the best were the people who leaned in to relationships,
blocks.zh_text: 过得最好的人，是那些用心投入人际关系的人，

blocks.en_text: with family, with friends, with community.
blocks.zh_text: 和家人、和朋友、和社区的关系。

blocks.en_text: So what about you?
blocks.zh_text: 那么你呢？

blocks.en_text: Let's say you're 25, or you're 40, or you're 60.
blocks.zh_text: 假设你25岁，或者40岁，或者60岁。

blocks.en_text: What might leaning in to relationships even look like?
blocks.zh_text: 用心投入人际关系，到底可以是什么样子呢？

blocks.en_text: Well, the possibilities are practically endless.
blocks.zh_text: 其实，可能性几乎无穷无尽。

blocks.en_text: It might be something as simple as replacing screen time with people time
blocks.zh_text: 它可能简单到只是把盯着屏幕的时间换成陪伴别人的时间，

blocks.en_text: or livening up a stale relationship by doing something new together,
blocks.zh_text: 或者一起做点新鲜事，让一段变得乏味的关系重新有活力，

blocks.en_text: long walks or date nights,
blocks.zh_text: 比如长时间散步，或者安排约会之夜，

blocks.en_text: or reaching out to that family member who you haven't spoken to in years,
blocks.zh_text: 或者主动联系那位你好多年没说过话的家人，

blocks.en_text: because those all-too-common family feuds
blocks.zh_text: 因为那些太常见的家庭不和

blocks.en_text: take a terrible toll
blocks.zh_text: 会带来可怕的代价，

blocks.en_text: on the people who hold the grudges.
blocks.zh_text: 代价落在那些心怀怨恨的人身上。

blocks.en_text: I'd like to close with a quote from Mark Twain.
blocks.zh_text: 我想用马克·吐温的一句话来结尾。

blocks.en_text: More than a century ago,
blocks.zh_text: 一个多世纪以前，

blocks.en_text: he was looking back on his life,
blocks.zh_text: 他回顾自己的一生，

blocks.en_text: and he wrote this:
blocks.zh_text: 写下了这段话：

blocks.en_text: "There isn't time, so brief is life,
blocks.zh_text: “人生如此短暂，没有时间

blocks.en_text: for bickerings, apologies, heartburnings, callings to account.
blocks.zh_text: 去争吵、去道歉、去伤心、去计较。

blocks.en_text: There is only time for loving,
blocks.zh_text: 只有时间去爱，

blocks.en_text: and but an instant, so to speak, for that."
blocks.zh_text: 而且可以说，去爱也只是一瞬间的事。”

blocks.en_text: The good life is built with good relationships.
blocks.zh_text: 美好的人生建立在良好的人际关系之上。

blocks.en_text: Thank you.
blocks.zh_text: 谢谢大家。
